text:
Alex K: heads-up, pager just hit for inference-prod prefix-thrash :rotating_light:
SRE-Bot: Pager triggered: inference-prod-high-latency (sev=2) — route: primary -> paging oncall
Jordan (oncall): I'm on it, grabbing logs and metric slices. Primary for next 30m is me, Mira you're secondary?
Mira P: yes I'm secondary, available for escalation. quick note: microshift tonight so short handoff at 00:30 UTC.
Alex K: impact? any customer-facing errors?
Jordan (oncall): initial look — 95th latency spiked to ~6s for small prompt sizes, error rate stable. seen on eu region and us-west. KV-cache hit-rate dropped to 10% from 78%.
Sam L: KV-cache drop rings true — saw a stale redis replica flip earlier in the hour in infra alerts. link to infra alert: https://redwood.internal/alerts/infra-9881
Lee C: if KV cache is low, we should avoid mass restarts. prefer rolling restart of cache-worker pool and warm cache. runbook here: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-warmup
Jordan (oncall): steps I'm executing now:
- check cache nodes: `kubectl get pods -n infra kv-cache --selector=app=kv-cache`
- check redis replication lag: `redis-cli -h redis-eu-01 info replication | grep lag`
- force warmup for hot prefixes via adhoc job

Alex K: paste logs/commands if you need help. Also add to handoff notes: possible recurring rota gap (microshift coverage shorter than usual).
Jordan (oncall): ran quick curl health against cache workers, several 502s. Restarting the 3 failing pods one at a time: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/kv-cache -n infra --selector=instance=eu-1`
Mira P: good, keep canary small. After restart, check prefix hit-rate and tail latency before doing us-west.
SRE-Bot: Deploy event: rollout restart started for deploy/kv-cache (eu-1) by Jordan (oncall)
Jordan (oncall): after first pod restart: prefix hit-rate up to 42%, 95th down to 2.1s. continuing with pod 2.
Sam L: pinging infra to confirm underlying disk IO spike earlier was mitigated. infra says they cleared a noisy backup job at 00:12 UTC. might explain lag.
Lee C: temporary mitigations checklist (short):
• avoid global restarts (use region canary)
• incremental restarts with 5m wait and perf check
• run quick warmup: `python tools/cache_warmup.py --prefix inference-prod --parallel 8`
• if warmup fails, flip routing to fallback model pool (route policy: fallback-quantized)
Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rapid-cache-mitigation

Jordan (oncall): second pod done — hit-rate 67%, 95th 1.1s. I'm going to let the rollout finish in eu and monitor 10m before touching us-west.
Alex K: record this on the shift log and include quick bullet steps for handoff. Mira, when you take over, confirm cold-start of workers in us-west before promoting primary.
Mira P: noted. I'll put this in the handoff: what I need from you is exact list of pods restarted and commands used. Also any follow-ups for infra.
Jordan (oncall): logging commands used in thread for handoff: 
```
kubectl get pods -n infra -l app=kv-cache
kubectl rollout restart deploy/kv-cache -n infra --selector=instance=eu-1
python tools/cache_warmup.py --prefix inference-prod --parallel 8
redis-cli -h redis-eu-01 info replication | grep lag
```
Also ticket to infra: INFRA-2321 (noisy backup) created by Sam L.
Sam L: INFRA-2321 link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INFRA-2321
Lee C: customer impact assessment quick notes:
- user-facing errors: none reported in SLOs (errors stayed ~0.2%)
- latency-sensitive customers (brownie corp) might see degraded UX; reach out if SLA threshold crossed
- recommended notify on-call pager channel if any errors >1% for >5m

Jordan (oncall): eu region stable after rollout. 95th 0.9s, hit-rate back to 82%. will watch for next 20m.
Alex K: great. Handoff plan for Mira: primary will move to Mira at 00:30 UTC. I'll remain reachable for 1 hour as adjacent support. In handoff note include: what fixed (redis lag + restarted eu cache pods), runbook links, commands run, INFRA ticket, suggested next steps (observe us-west, consider cache replica rotation if recurrence).
Mira P: copying checklist into handoff channel now. Quick checklist entry for whoever picks up next microshift:
- check redis replication lag and CPU/io metrics
- verify cache hit-rate >60% before promoting region primary
- avoid global cache restarts; use canary restarts
- warmup top 100 prefixes after restarts
- contact infra on INFRA-2321 if backups still scheduled

Jordan (oncall): adding final note: if latency resurges and warmup isn't enough, fallback action is to flip routing to fallback-quantized model pool with this command: `curl -XPOST https://console.internal/routes/switch -d '{"route":"fallback-quantized"}'` (ops only).
Mira P: ack. I'll monitor and escalate if anything crosses the impact threshold. thanks team :thumbsup:
Alex K: nice microshift handling, Jordan. I'll include these bullet points in the runbook quick-snippets doc for microshifts.
SRE-Bot: Pager resolved for inference-prod-high-latency (auto-resolved)
Jordan (oncall): closing my active tasks, leaving handoff note in /handoffs/microshift/2778883333.md and marking primary->Mira at 00:30 UTC.
Mira P: received and annotated. Taking primary at 00:30. leaving this thread for record.
Sam L: postmortem / follow-ups: check weekly scheduled backup windows and add guard on noisy jobs.
Lee C: extra action: add a small alert on KV cache failed ops >3% for 5m so we catch earlier. runbook pointer included above.
Alex K: thanks all, stand down unless it fires again.
